title: Whichever checkout releases a cell clears the rows that cell owns, capped or not
action: Two defects on the release side, both about the same wrong question. FIRST: the holder filter. In release.rs, search for the line that skips a hold unless its holder equals the acting topology holder; the cap-time copy of the same loop is in cells/finish_support.rs (search it for the same holder comparison). Both ask the acting checkout. Ask hha-1's helper for the cell being released instead, so whichever checkout runs the release clears the rows that cell's owner holds — this matters because `cells finish` typically runs from MAIN (finish_support.rs says so itself, search for `MAIN checkout` in its comments) while hha-1 now stamps the worktree. SECOND: reachability. Release derives the {cell, session} pairs it scopes the ledger pass by from LIVE reservations for the agent (search release.rs for `matched rows FIRST`). Once the cell is capped or unclaimed those leases are gone, the pairs are empty, and the rows become unreachable by any release — that is why ghost rows outlive the cells that made them. When an explicit --cell is given, scope the ledger pass by that cell id directly instead of only through the derived pairs. Note the blast radius and keep it honest: release_exec is also reached by release_reservations_for_agent from verbs/drivers/prepare.rs (search prepare.rs for that name) on the claim-unwind path, so those unwinds get the wider scoping too. Keep the session match, keep the lock, keep holds_released counting exactly the rows it marked.

truths: release --agent A --cell C marks C's matching ledger rows released even when no lease for C exists any more
A release run from main for a cell owned by a granted worktree clears that cell's worktree-stamped rows
cells finish run from main clears the rows of the cell it caps
release without --cell clears exactly what it clears today
holds_released counts exactly the rows it marked

artifacts.substantive: the holder filter resolved through the cell-ownership helper, and the ledger pass scoped by an explicit --cell independently of live reservations
the cap-time release loop's holder filter resolved the same way
red-first cases for the orphaned row with no lease, and for a main-run release clearing a worktree-owned cell's rows

key_links: both release paths ask who owns the cell, not who typed the command
an explicit --cell reaches the ledger without a live reservation to derive it from
prohibitions: Do not let a checkout clear rows belonging to a cell it does not own
Do not make release without --cell clear anything it does not clear today
Do not drop or move the store lock around the ledger write

trace.outcome: release_exec and finish_support's cap-time release now filter ledger rows through cell_hold_owner (the cell's owner) instead of the acting checkout's topology holder, and an explicit --cell appends a session-less pair so the ledger pass reaches rows whose leases are already gone.
